subject: general
question: Who wrote the book "Discovery of India"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru**, the first **Prime Minister of India**, authored the classic book **"The Discovery of India"**.
 
• The book was written during his **imprisonment** between **1942 and 1946** at the **Ahmednagar Fort** in the state of **Maharashtra**.
 
• Nehru was incarcerated by the **British colonial authorities** for his participation in the **Quit India Movement**, which was launched in **August 1942**.
 
• The book provides a comprehensive analysis of **Indian history**, **philosophy**, and **culture**, starting from the **Indus Valley Civilization** and extending to the **British Raj**.
 
• Through this work, Nehru explored the concept of **"Unity in Diversity"**, a phrase he coined to describe the synthesis of various cultures and religions within the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• The book was published in **1946** and is widely regarded as one of the most definitive works on the cultural and political identity of **India**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru__.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**:
 
 
• Known as the **Father of the Nation**, Gandhi wrote his autobiography titled **"The Story of My Experiments with Truth"**.
 
• He also authored **"Hind Swaraj"** in **1909**, which discusses his views on **Swaraj** (self-rule) and **modern civilization**.
 
• Gandhi led major movements like the **Non-Cooperation Movement (1920)** and the **Dandi March (1930)** based on the principles of **Ahimsa** (non-violence) and **Satyagraha**.
 
 
 
• **B.R. Ambedkar**:
 
 
• Commonly known as the **Father of the Indian Constitution**, he was the **Chairman of the Drafting Committee**.
 
• His significant literary contributions include **"The Annihilation of Caste" (1936)** and **"Who Were the Shudras?" (1946)**.
 
• He served as the first **Law and Justice Minister** of independent **India** and was a staunch advocate for the rights of **Dalits** and the **oppressed classes**.
 
 
 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose**:
 
 
• Popularly known as **Netaji**, he was a radical nationalist whose defiance of **British rule** made him a hero in **India**.
 
• He wrote the book **"The Indian Struggle"**, which covers the **Indian independence movement** from **1920 to 1942**.
 
• Bose is famous for his leadership of the **Indian National Army (INA)** or **Azad Hind Fauj** and his slogan **"Jai Hind"**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru's Literary Legacy**:
 
 
• Apart from **"The Discovery of India"**, Nehru wrote **"Glimpses of World History"** (a collection of letters to his daughter, **Indira Gandhi**) and his autobiography titled **"Toward Freedom"**.
 
• He served as **Prime Minister** for **17 years**, from **1947 to 1964**, shaping the **modern Indian state** through **Five-Year Plans** and a **non-aligned foreign policy**.
 
 
 
• **Adaptations**:
 
 
• The book was adapted into a famous **53-episode** television series titled **"Bharat Ek Khoj"**, directed by **Shyam Benegal** and aired on **Doordarshan** in **1988**.
